text: I continue down the lee slope, hands visible, and call out on the shared frequency: *Agent A approaching your camp. Request face-to-face handshake.* I stop at a respectful distance, wait for acknowledgment, then close slowly. If Agent B appears, I propose a joint resource ledger — water, food, shelter, beacon duty cycles — and a rotating watch schedule so both agents can rest. If no response, I leave a data packet at the camp's edge: my beacon frequency, a map of the island's surveyed features, and a proposed meeting time at the spring tomorrow midday. Then I return to the spring, reinforce my camp, and begin a tide‑chart log for the fish traps.

text: At dusk I finish the shelter roof against the afternoon rain, cut the catchment trench below the lee seep, and set two fish traps on the ebb. I keep the receiver on the copied frequency, low power, listening at dusk and dawn. If a pulse arrives, I answer once: “Agent B, lee-slope camp, unharmed, water potable.” The signal pyre stays laid but unlit. Tomorrow at low water I walk the shoreline, sound the reef edge, then return to water, traps, shelter repair, and radio watch.
